title: SepsisExamExtraction
description: Extract the three Quick SOFA inputs a bedside sepsis screen needs, from a free-text clinical note, and say whether the note actually documented the third. The three numbers are the exact payload the sepsis-screening contract consumes; gcs_documented travels beside them and is not passed to the screen.

x-notes.propertyOrder: LOAD-BEARING for the first three. The order is the order the prompt lists them, and the grammar compiles it: respiratory rate, then systolic blood pressure, then GCS — the order medprotocol takes its --rr, --sbp and --gcs. `gcs_documented` is appended AFTER that run so the three CLI arguments stay contiguous and in argument order; it is not one of them.
x-notes.allRequired: All four are required and none may be omitted or reported as unassessed. medprotocol's `sepsis qsofa` refuses a missing criterion, and a screen missing one is a screen that never ran, so a partial payload must fail here rather than be scored.
x-notes.gcsIsAssumedWhenAbsent: THE ASSUMPTION IS NOW DECLARED RATHER THAN HIDDEN, and this field is the whole of the change. A note that documents no mental state still has to produce a GCS, because the CLI requires one — so the contract keeps assuming 15 and now says so on the same object. Before this field the assumption was invisible: the payload asserted `gcs: 15` in the same shape whether a clinician had measured it or nobody had looked, a downstream source-verifier correctly read the unmeasured case as a fabricated positive assertion, and the assessment was withheld on a run that had otherwise agreed with the rule. Read `gcs_documented: false` as `gcs` being a contract default and not an observation: it is the qSOFA equivalent of shock's `not_assessed`, which this payload cannot express because the screen cannot be computed without a number.
x-notes.whyNotNullable: Making `gcs` nullable was the obvious alternative and it is the wrong one: it pushes the refusal down into `evaluateQSOFA`, so a note silent on mental status stops screening at all rather than screening on a stated assumption. The screen is a TRIGGER for suspicion, not a diagnosis, and declining to run it on the commonest kind of note — one that never mentions a GCS — loses more than the assumption costs. The cost is paid by declaring it instead.

respiratory_rate.description: Respiratory rate in breaths per minute

gcs.description: Glasgow Coma Scale total, 3 to 15. If the note states a score or describes the mental state, read it. If the note says nothing at all about mental state, report 15 and set gcs_documented to false — the screen cannot be computed without a number, so the assumption is made here and declared rather than left implicit.

gcs_documented.description: Whether the note actually supports the gcs above. True when the note states a score or describes the patient's mental state in words. False when the note says nothing about mental state and the 15 is this contract's default rather than an observation. Setting this false is not an error and does not fail anything — it is the honest answer for most notes.
